summary.content:
Today's selection covers 77 articles from 8 trusted sources, including 52 on Artificial Intelligence and 13 on Fraud/Cybersecurity.

• **AI Spotlight**: OpenAI Introduces ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ as Safety Concerns Grow
• **Companies in Focus**: Coverage includes developments from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic
• **Security Alert**: CISA: Windows Task Host flaw now exploited by ransomware gangs
• **Threat Landscape**: Today's coverage highlights ransomware, data breaches, malware
• **Source Diversity**: Articles sourced from NY Times Tech, The Verge, BBC Technology, TechCrunch, BleepingComputer and others
• **Fresh Content**: 49 articles published in the last 24 hours

top.title: OpenAI Introduces ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ as Safety Concerns Grow
top.description: The artificial intelligence start-up announced a chatbot mode that will automatically limit some conversations to better protect young users.

top.title: The Blackout That Could Devastate America
top.description: The power grid relies on thousands of aging, hand-built transformers. If enough fail, the blackout could last years.

top.description: OpenAI is announcing security updates following the July news that its AI broke out of a sandboxed environment and accidentally hacked Hugging Face, including improvements to its research environments...

top.title: OpenAI makes ChatGPT less 'human' for teens in new safety update
top.description: OpenAI insisted this was not in response to a particular issue with children believing ChatGPT to be alive.

top.description: The new safeguards include more detailed monitoring of models during the development process, as well as greater emphasis on alignment and security during the post-training process.

top.title: OpenAI launches a safer ChatGPT for teens — years after teens started using it
top.description: ChatGPT for Teens adds age-appropriate safety measures, parental controls, and learning tools designed to steer teens away from harmful content — and from using AI to cheat on their homework.
